name: Agent Run Review
summary: One agent run, reviewable end to end: a Plan with its decision contract, an AgentTimeline whose last step follows your answer, a Tool call with arguments and result one click away, a ToolResultCard hosting the chart the run produced, TokenUsage in the header and an ApprovalCard for the one side effect that waits for a human. Reports the decision through onDecision and never performs it.
question: What did the agent do, and what is it asking me?

name: AI Chart
summary: Renders a model's chart tool-output inside an AI conversation — AutoChart (@elabs-ai/components-charts) composed with Tool/ToolOutput from @elabs-ai/components-ai. The canonical copy-owned home for @elabs-ai/components-ai + @elabs-ai/components-charts cross-sibling composition.

name: AI Chat Shell
summary: Chat surface with transcript, composer, tool calls and a context rail.

name: Annotated Trend
summary: "What happened, and when?" — a 20-week LineChart with up to three labelled events anchored to the exact data point they explain, connected by a Leader, never a legend. Compact keeps only the most consequential event.
question: What happened, and when?

name: Area Against a Threshold
summary: A whole published figure: one line against a labelled threshold, the area between them filled in one colour below and another above, both sides named on the plot, a final-value note, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.
question: Since when are we over the line?

name: Area multiples
summary: Small-multiple area charts on one shared scale: a dotted network average behind every panel, the same shaded event, and the latest value in each panel title.
question: How do I compare the same measure across regions without a spaghetti chart?

name: Area Stat
summary: KPI stat card with a live area chart sparkline, hover-driven value/label updates, and a tokenized trend badge.

name: Arrow plot with target band
summary: An arrow plot: one arrow per row coloured by direction, percent deltas, a shaded target band and a computed headline.
question: How do I show which rows improved and which got worse?

name: Audit Log
summary: An append-only audit table whose actor column tells three authors apart by glyph — copilot, delegated agent, person — and whose result column is a status badge with an icon (Applied / Held / Stopped / Reverted), so a row still reads in greyscale. Monospace tabular timestamps; the action is one plain sentence with the number it wrote in it.
question: Who did what?

name: Before After
summary: "Who improved, who slipped?" — a DumbbellChart slope chart of 6 depots, Q2 → Q3, with the biggest riser and biggest faller emphasised and every other depot on a shared muted line; direction is carried by the line's own slope, never colour alone.
question: Who improved, who slipped?

name: Bento
summary: A BentoGrid of product proof where each tile shows the thing: a live AreaChart, a Meter, a Sparkline, status badges.

name: Billing
summary: Plan and renewal, usage Meters with an included-amount marker and overage in words, the card by its last four digits, and an invoices Table.

name: Bubble Almanac
summary: A category × category matrix drawn as hand-irregular blob bubbles on ruled ledger paper, with a margin note calling out the busiest cell (PeakRing + Marginalia). One-off editorial composition adapted from lieflat-charts' 'L9 Bubble Almanac'.

name: Bubble chart
summary: A bubble scatter on a log axis: size by head count, colour by region with a key, a dashed trend, selective point labels and a text annotation.
question: How do I relate two measures across many items, and name only the outliers?

name: Calendar heatmap
summary: A calendar heatmap: weeks as columns, weekdays as rows, six sequential steps and a key that states each range.
question: How do I show a daily number for a whole year?

name: Call to Action
summary: The closing ask: one primary action, one quieter alternative and what trying it costs.

name: Chart and Table
summary: ChartFrame (expand / flip-to-table / download-CSV) wired to @elabs-ai/components-data: full TanStack DataTable on flip and downloadCsv on export.

name: Chart Card
summary: An elevated chart-in-a-card: a header with a headline KPI + delta + a segmented period control (ToggleGroup), a token-coloured AreaChart, and a footer breakdown legend. The period control re-renders the chart.

name: Checkout
summary: One-page checkout with autocomplete on every field, errors after the first attempt with focus moved to the first, a delivery RadioGroup that changes the total, and a slot for the payment provider's hosted card field.

name: Choropleth Stat
summary: KPI stat card with a choropleth world-map chart, hover-driven country value/label updates, and a tokenized trend badge.

name: Code Workspace
summary: Multi-file Monaco code editor with brand-ui tabs and token theming (wire @elabs-ai/components-editor/monaco-environment once at the app entry).

name: Cohort Retention
summary: "Do customers stay?" — a triangular cohort retention heatmap: one row per monthly signup cohort, one column per month since signup, shaded by the share still active. A cohort younger than N months draws an empty cell, never a fabricated zero. One cohort is called out with a peak ring and a stated, computed gap against its named peers.
question: Do customers stay?

name: Column panels with ranges
summary: Two column panels on one shared axis, with the promoter and detractor ranges of the scale shaded and named, and a computed share in each panel title.
question: How do I compare two distributions on a rating scale?

name: Composition
summary: "What is it made of?" — a 100%-stacked segmented bar per card (revenue by channel, shipments by region) plus a legend list that is the accessible source of truth: label, share, absolute value, and the share's own change vs last year in pp. Bar and legend share one order and a rank number so colour is never the only link between a segment and its row; shares under 3% merge into "Other".
question: What is it made of?

name: Contact
summary: A short validated contact form with a topic Select, a personal confirmation and the other ways to reach the team.

name: Data Table
summary: Filterable, sortable, paginated TanStack data table with toolbar.

name: Decision Record
summary: Every AI action expanded into the reason it happened: what it did, what it looked at (named, openable evidence), what rule applied (the clause, monospace), how confident (or an honest "not applicable"), and how to reverse it. Below: the check list (confirmed / not confirmed) and what the copilot proposes — numbered, editable, nothing actioned until a person approves.
question: Why did the AI do that?

name: Dependency Web
summary: "What depends on what?" — a platform's call graph as a NetworkChart (node size is traffic, colour is tier) beside the same services as a TreeChart of ownership. The headline counts inbound links and names the service most others lean on.
question: What depends on what?

name: Distribution
summary: "Is it consistent?" — an average hides the tail: a median headline next to p90/p95 read against a named SLA threshold, a box plot of the record-level distribution with the threshold drawn as a reference line, and the share past it stated in text.
question: Is it consistent?

name: Diverging Bars
summary: A whole published figure: signed horizontal bars from a shared zero line, gains and losses in two colours keyed inside the description, signed value labels, a row note beside the outlier, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.
question: Who is ahead, who is behind, and by how much?

name: Diverging Columns
summary: A whole published figure: columns above and below zero in two colours whose key is written into the description, a note on the low point, signed axis, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.
question: When did it turn, and when did it turn back?

name: Donut with total
summary: A donut with the total in the hole, outside labels on leaders stating name and share, and small slices folded into Other.
question: How do I show what one number is made of?

name: Donuts then and now
summary: Two donuts under one shared colour key: the year in the hole, shares inside the slices, the same slice order in both.
question: How do I compare the same split at two points in time?

name: Dot plot with range
summary: A dot plot: three dots per row joined by their range, a colour key, a top value axis and rows sorted by the headline value.
question: How do I compare three values per row on one axis?

name: Dual axis columns and line
summary: Columns on the left axis and a line on the right: axes coloured like their series, ticks aligned on shared gridlines, a shaded range, and a table tooltip.
question: How do I show volume and unit cost in one figure?

name: Empty States
summary: Six empty and error states on StatePanel with the library's illustrations — first run, no results, an empty list that is good news, error, offline, no access — each saying what happened, whether anything is lost and the way out.

name: Escalation Boundary
summary: The one dial an AI-ops product must put on screen: a stacked distribution bar of every decision by how well it was corroborated, with the evidence threshold drawn as a mark; the evidence ladder (countable tick meter, meaning, decisions, share, side); and three "If you move it" scenario cards that state the trade in the reader’s units (cleared share, queue delta, catches, reviews per catch) and MOVE the boundary when clicked.
question: Where does autonomy end?

name: FAQ
summary: An Accordion of pre-sale questions beside a person to ask.

name: Features
summary: A SectionHeader plus a FeatureGrid of six outcome-led reasons.

name: Finding Cards
summary: Recoverable-spend findings as a row of cards: a status badge naming the kind, a one-line title, the recoverable figure as the only coloured number (kpi-sm), a two-sentence summary and a primary + secondary action, under a header that states the programme and the total the cards add up to. The primary action is what a person signs; the secondary always opens the evidence.
question: What did the copilot find?

name: Fleet Tracker
summary: A fleet where it is: each vehicle's planned route as a dashed MapRoute, the part already driven solid, the vehicle's MapMarker at the join and the depot marked; the list shows stops done on a Meter and minutes against plan, and selecting a vehicle fades the others.
question: Where is everyone, and who is late?

name: Flow Builder
summary: Workflow-builder canvas with a node palette, auto-layout, grouping, placeholder growth, insert-between, an inspector, and copy-own undo/redo + copy/paste.

name: Flow Canvas
summary: Branded React Flow canvas with custom nodes, edges and controls.

name: Footer
summary: One-line positioning, three labelled nav columns and the legal row.

name: Forecast
summary: "Where will I land?" — a linear run-rate projection to the end of the quarter: solid actual, dashed projection, a ±1σ confidence range that widens toward period end, a labelled target line and a today marker separating the two, with the projection method stated in words.
question: Where will I land?

name: Forgot Password
summary: Asks for the email and answers the same way whether or not the account exists; the confirmation names the address, the link's lifetime and the way back.

name: Form Wizard
summary: A multi-step form with a horizontal numbered stepper (the Wizard primitive) — a checkout flow (Customer → Shipping → Payment → Review) with real fields, correct autocomplete/type hints, and a Descriptions review step.

name: Gap To Benchmark
summary: "How far from the benchmark?" — a sorted DumbbellChart, one row per depot, hollow benchmark marker vs filled actual marker, worst gap first, with the widest gaps emphasised; the gap's sign correctly flips for a lower-is-better metric.
question: How far from the benchmark?

name: Handoff Inspector
summary: One edge of a multi-agent run: sender → a metric pill on the arrow (context size, latency, tokens, fields present of required) → receiver; a context-comparison table (sent vs expected, status badge per field) that shows the required field that was not sent; the payload size against the workflow baseline as a Meter with a marker; and the edge’s 24-hour health beside it.
question: Where was the context dropped?

name: Heat table
summary: A heat table: a depot by weekday matrix with printed values, five sequential steps, a key that states each range and the maximum ringed.
question: How do I show every number and still let the pattern show first?

name: Hero
summary: Landing hero section with eyebrow, headline, CTAs and logo strip.

name: Hero and Satellites
summary: "What is the headline?" — one hero KPI (a big value, a named comparison vs target, a 13-week trend against last year) with three compact satellite KPIs beside it, each a value + signed delta vs target + a tiny trend, composed as one card with a single separation gesture.
question: What is the headline?

name: Highlighted Columns
summary: A whole published figure: grey context columns, the columns after the event in the accent colour with value labels, an arrowed note naming the event, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.
question: What changed, and since when?

name: Highlighted Lines
summary: A whole published figure: three named, coloured lines in front of a field of thin grey ones, names at the line ends, a note in the series colour, hover that lifts one line, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.
question: Which few stand out from the many?

name: Hourglass Stream
summary: A funnel redrawn as counted barcode strips (UnitStack) with trickle threads (DrawPath) narrowing between stages, plus stage-to-stage conversion callouts. One-off editorial composition adapted from lieflat-charts' 'L13 Hourglass Stream', built entirely from @elabs-ai/components-charts' marks layer.

name: Insight Feed
summary: The AI-ops briefing pattern: a numbered feed of things the copilot did or noticed — a one-sentence fact, a paragraph of why, the evidence it read, its confidence and two actions — with a conflict item that carries no confidence ("No verdict — a person decides"). Beside it, a "Needs a person" rail of what stopped and a "Derivation load" split of applied / sent to you / pinned by people.
question: What changed while you were away?

name: Integration Grid
summary: A responsive grid of integration cards (icon + name + description + connect/manage action + connection status) under a page header with an Add action — the canonical ‘connect your tools’ surface. Logos are consumer-supplied (Lucide placeholders here).

name: Journey Flow
summary: "Where do they drop off?" — a SankeyChart from the channel a request came in on, through what happened to its quote, to how it ended, with a FunnelChart beside it that counts each step. The headline names the channel that loses the largest share of its own requests.
question: Where do they drop off?

name: Kanban Board
summary: Drag cards between columns or use each card's Move menu (keyboard, screen reader and touch), with a live-region announcement, per-column points and WIP-limit warnings in words.

name: KPI Provenance Strip
summary: "Where the business stands" — four headline figures on ONE surface, each with an inline signed delta and the line that earns the number its place: source and freshness ("ERP · 2 min ago", "Derived from 61 open orders · 06:02"). Peers separated by hairlines, no value without provenance; the delta is secondary (arrow + sign, never colour alone).
question: Where does this number come from?

name: Launch Plan
summary: A launch on one screen: the Gantt carries the plan with summary rows, dependencies, a baseline under the task that slipped, a milestone and markers for today and go-live; selecting a task spells out its dates, baseline, what it waits for and its progress in a Descriptions panel. The headline counts the days left and the tasks past baseline.
question: Will we make the date, and what is in the way?

name: Line Stat
summary: KPI stat card with an inline line chart, hover-driven value/label updates, and a tokenized trend badge.

name: Line With Events
summary: A whole published figure: one long weekly line over shaded peak seasons, dashed and dotted event lines, a target line, an arrowed note on the record low, a notes line that explains the shading, byline, linked source and Get the data.
question: What happened, and what did it cost?

name: Lines With Projection
summary: A whole published figure: two crossing lines named at their ends, a shaded and labelled plan range in which the lines turn dashed, an arrowed note at the crossing, the colour key written into the description, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.
question: When do they cross, and how much of that is forecast?

name: Live Ops Wall
summary: An operations wall that moves: a LiveLineChart streaming one reading a second, three Gauge dials with their targets on the dial, a Timeline of what the on-call already knows, services sorted worst first with a Sparkline and a status badge each, and a HeatmapChart of when the load arrives. The headline is computed from the services; paused freezes the stream.
question: What is happening right now, and what needs me?

name: Login
summary: Sign in with email and password plus brand-neutral other ways in. Field errors after the first attempt, a revealable password, a pending button and the server's answer as an alert; hands the values to onSubmit and never calls a server itself.

name: Login Split
summary: The sign-in form beside a brand panel painted with the primary pair. Container-query layout: the panel stands down when narrow.

name: Market Tape
summary: A rate desk: a tape of lanes across the top with price, move and a 20-day Sparkline each, over a CandlestickChart of the index and a BarChart of daily volume. Every move carries an arrow and a sign as well as a colour; the chart title is computed from the first open and the last close.
question: Where is the market, and what moved it?

name: Members
summary: Members with in-place role changes, a protected owner, an invite dialog that checks address, duplicates and seats, pending invites in the same list and a confirming remove.

name: Movers
summary: "What changed most?" — the top 3 risers and top 3 fallers in a ranked depot field (on-time delivery, revenue), each row stating its rank, how many places it moved, and a diverging mini bar from a shared, stated zero axis. Distinct from stat-list-01's single-snapshot share bars: this is about movement between two points in time.
question: What changed most?

name: Multi-baseline
summary: "Compared to what?" — one wide card per KPI stacking three named baselines (target, last year, budget), each with a shared-scale dot strip so the same number's distance to every reference reads at a glance.
question: Compared to what?

name: Navbar
summary: Site navigation: links inline when there is room and in a Sheet when there is not, aria-current on the active route, container-query layout.

name: Network Map
summary: A network on the map it runs on: MapCanvas in globe projection with one MapArc per lane, its width bound to volume through a paint expression, hubs as MapMarkers with tooltips, and a panel that ranks the lanes with a Meter and calls out the late ones. Selecting a lane on the map or in the list dims the rest and redraws that arc heavier.
question: Where does the volume flow, and which lane is late?

name: Newsletter
summary: One field, a promise about frequency, validation and a confirmation that names the address.

name: Notifications
summary: An events-by-channels matrix as a real table of Switches with full accessible names, locked cells that say why, and a count of events that reach you nowhere.

name: Onboarding Checklist
summary: A getting-started checklist that opens on the next step, says how long each takes, counts the minutes left on a Meter and ends with a closing state.

name: Order Receipt
summary: The confirmation page: order number, arrival, address, lines and what happens next as a Timeline.

name: Pace
summary: "Will I make it by period end?" — quarter-to-date Progress bars with a marker for the expected pace and a computed days-ahead/behind status, plus a Gauge card reading a rate KPI against its target and thresholds.
question: Will I make it by period end?

name: Pareto
summary: A Pareto chart: sorted columns on the left axis and the labelled cumulative share on the right, with a computed headline.
question: Which few causes make up most of the problem?

name: Part To Whole
summary: "Where does the money go?" — a two-level treemap of Q3 cost, category → sub-category, drawn in one neutral mono shade except for the single highlighted tile, outlined and named with a Leader + HaloText callout stating its share and the change from last quarter. Tile area is exactly proportional to cost.
question: Where does the money go?

name: Pricing
summary: Three plans named for who they are for, a billing toggle that recomputes every price, locale-aware currency and a featured plan marked in words.

name: Process Explorer
summary: A map-first process-mining workspace over an order-to-cash log: the six KPIs as one ribbon, every control in a toolbar so nothing floats over the map, and beside the map a panel of statistical insights — throughput distribution against the SLA, the slowest hand-overs, the weekly trend, box and violin plots by region and channel — plus variants as colour strips, the selected element and deviations. A dock holds the dotted chart, the performance spectrum, the workload heatmap and the case table; a replay animates every order as a token. One useProcessExplorer instance drives all of it, so no two panels can disagree.
question: Where does the process really go, and where does it wait?

name: Product Detail
summary: A product page with required options (the button names the missing one), a stock-capped quantity, delivery promises, a Rating and details in an Accordion.

name: Product Grid
summary: A product listing with a category filter, sorting and cards that state markdowns and stock in words; sold-out products cannot be added.

name: Profile
summary: A profile form with dirty tracking (the save bar appears only when something changed), validation on save, a counted bio and a danger zone behind a ConfirmDialog that names what is lost.

name: Profile Compare
summary: "How do the options compare?" — a RadarChart with one shape per option across five scored promises, beside a ParallelCoordinatesChart of the raw measures behind the scores. The headline names the strongest profile and the promise it is weakest on.
question: How do the options compare?

name: Project Cards
summary: Projects as cards with progress against time on one Meter (marker = today), a derived health word, team avatars, due date and a counted state filter.

name: Provenance Record
summary: A record whose every field says where its value came from: derived (confidence meter + evidence kind), pinned (who and when — a pin out-ranks any derivation), conflict (two permitted sources disagree; nothing chosen) or empty ("No signal yet" — never a guess). Each state has its own glyph + text, and the footer counts the four so the reader knows how much of the record is machine-derived.
question: Where did each field come from?

name: Radial Patchwork
summary: Events on a 24 h clock face, density shown by overlaid translucent sectors (fill-opacity 0.07–0.16 — the one sanctioned use of transparency in this system) with rim ticks and a category legend. One-off editorial composition adapted from lieflat-charts' 'L10 Radial Patchwork'.

name: Range Bars
summary: A whole published figure: a range plot drawn with bar overlays — fastest to slowest, the middle half and a median tick per row on one shared axis, with its key above the plot, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.
question: How wide is the spread, and where is the typical case?

name: Range plot with deltas
summary: A grouped range plot: hollow before, filled after, a signed delta per row, group headers and a top value axis.
question: How do I show before and after per row, and how much it moved?

name: Ranked Bars
summary: A whole published figure: ranked horizontal bars on a track to 100 %, the three lowest and three highest rows in colour and the rest as grey context, a colour key above the plot, values inside the bars, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.
question: Who is at the top, and who is at the bottom?

name: Ratio and Unit
summary: "How big is it in human terms?" — a rate restated as a small, countable fraction ("1 in 12 orders arrived late") via UnitChart, with the exact rate spelled out beneath the rounded headline and a comparison vs last year. Highlighted units use an accent fill against a neutral rest rather than hue alone.
question: How big is it in human terms?

name: Register
summary: Create an account: name, work email, a password with a strength meter that names the unmet rules, and explicit consent. Errors appear after the first attempt.

name: Reset Password
summary: Choose a new password: whose account, strength explained, the two entries compared, and an end state that says other sessions were signed out.

name: Revenue Desk
summary: A revenue desk in one block: a MetricGrid of four headline numbers that each name their baseline and carry a 13-week Sparkline, a ComposedChart of weekly revenue with its trailing average against a labelled plan rule, a donut PieChart of the service-line mix, a BumpChart of which line is climbing, and the accounts that decide the quarter with a Meter each. Container-query layout, so it holds in a dashboard column and on a full page.
question: How is the quarter going, and what decides it?

name: Score Explanation
summary: A scored decision decomposed into its signals: one row per signal, a signed bar whose length is the contribution in points and whose direction is the sign — ink for positive, the warning rung for negative, each with a signed number so the sign never rides on colour. One shared zero-based scale; the footer states how many weaker signals were considered but not shown.
question: Why is the score 91?

name: Scorecard
summary: The Power BI-style scorecard, done with an honest baseline on every number: one row per KPI — actual, target, a signed delta, a BulletChart progress-to-target, a 13-week trend, and a named status — in a horizontally scrollable Table.
question: Give me the whole picture in one table.

name: Seasons as Dots and Lines
summary: A whole published figure: twenty seasons of daily readings as small dots coloured by decade, two average lines and the current year on top, the colour key carried by the title's own words, two notes on the cloud, method note, byline and linked source.
question: Is this year unusual, and is the decade?

name: Shopping Cart
summary: Stock-capped quantities, remove with undo, a discount code that answers either way, progress to free delivery on a Meter and totals that add up.

name: Small Multiples
summary: "Which depot is the outlier?" — twelve depots, one tiny 13-week line per tile, every tile on the same shared y-axis so height compares directly, with the one depot that stands out ringed and coloured (PeakRing) while every other depot stays on a muted neutral.
question: Which one is the outlier?

name: Spend Against Limit
summary: Every non-human spender on the card programme, sorted by share of ceiling: monospace agent id, autonomy band as a status badge (Auto / Review / Hold), a bar with the ceiling drawn as a vertical mark, the literal "$612 of $500", and Revoke. Over the ceiling paints the destructive rung and says so. Above it, three autonomy-band tiles total the envelopes per band.
question: How close is each agent to its ceiling?

name: Stacked Among Plain Bars
summary: A whole published figure: one ranked list where the comparison rows are plain grey bars and the rows the story is about are stacked by component, with totals, a colour key, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.
question: How big is it next to everything else, and what is it made of?

name: Stat Grid
summary: Elevated KPI tiles beyond a flat number: MetricCard + inline Sparkline (bar or line, coloured by a --chart-* token), a goal/progress tile, and a this-vs-last comparison tile.

name: Stat List
summary: Compact summary widgets: a ranked list with share bars + delta (Sales by country), a leaderboard (Top performers), and a transaction/activity feed with signed amounts.

name: Stats and Logos
summary: A StatsBand of the numbers over a LogoStrip of who stands behind them.

name: Status Threshold
summary: "Should I act?" — a status (icon + text, never colour alone) read against a visible on-track/at-risk/off-track threshold scale with today's value marked, plus how long the current status has held.
question: Should I act?

name: Streak
summary: "How reliable is it?" — a ratio/streak headline over a 30-day strip of day cells, missed days marked by shape as well as colour, with the current and longest streaks and a comparison to the prior 30 days.
question: How reliable is it?

name: Table with bars and sparklines
summary: A scorecard table: bar cells, a shaded heat column, category dots, sparklines with the last point emphasised and signed, coloured change.
question: How do I make a table readable at a glance?

name: Target Bullet
summary: "Am I on target?" — a grid of KPI cards, each a BulletChart (value against target, last year, and 2–3 qualitative bands) plus a named comparison row and an as-of footnote. A lower-is-better KPI states that its bands read best-to-worst in reverse.
question: Am I on target?

name: Team
summary: Names, roles and one line about each person; container-query columns.

name: Terminal Session Idle
summary: A settled coding-agent console: launch banner, transcript, composer with mode/effort indicator, status bar. Nothing is running.

name: Terminal Session Mid-turn
summary: A coding-agent console under way: tool calls, a diff hunk, a working line with a stop affordance, a pending permission prompt, status bar.

name: Testimonials
summary: A masonry wall of quotes with name, role and a read-only Rating.

name: Todo List
summary: Add with Enter, tick to complete, filter, clear completed; the header counts open and overdue tasks and every control names the task it acts on.

name: Trace Waterfall
summary: An execution waterfall for one multi-agent run: a stat strip where every number carries its comparison (duration vs p95, retries, tokens in/out, cost vs workflow average, failed at), the charts package’s Gantt at sub-second granularity with one row per agent span nested under its caller, and a context-flow chain that shows the hop where a required field was dropped.
question: Where did the run fail?

name: Trend Reference
summary: "Better or worse than normal?" — a 13-week Sparkline trend read against a target pace, last year, and a normal operating band, with a text legend spelling out the line styles so the encoding never rides on colour alone.
question: Better or worse than normal?

name: Two Factor
summary: Six digits in one InputOTP that submits itself when full, a resend that counts down, and a recovery-code way out.

name: Variance Bridge
summary: "What drove the change?" — a revenue bridge from last quarter's total to this quarter's, split into price, volume, mix, FX and other, built with WaterfallChart and a Leader callout on the one or two steps that actually explain the move. Steps sum exactly to the ending total; every step states its own sign in words, never colour alone.
question: What drove the change?

name: Verdict Side By Side
summary: A keep-vs-cancel verdict side by side: two cards on the success/destructive washes with annual cost, a segmented seat-utilisation Meter and the deciding facts; a one-line reading of the comparison; “If you cancel” as four consequence stats; “How the copilot knows” as a numbered evidence list; and the refusal — the copilot prepares everything, a person signs.
question: Keep this, cancel that?

name: Verify Email
summary: The waiting room after sign-up: which address, what to do, a counting-down resend and the way back for a mistyped address.

name: Waterfall bridge
summary: A revenue bridge: coloured increases and decreases between two totals, thin connectors, matched-colour labels and a callout on the step that matters.
question: How did one total become another?

name: Waterfall with subtotals
summary: A horizontal waterfall: monthly steps, automatic quarterly subtotals, a closing total and a plot zoomed to the differences.
question: How do I show a year of monthly changes with quarterly checkpoints?

name: AreaChart
summary: Cumulative or part-of-whole trend over time — a filled line.

name: AutoChart
summary: Spec-driven chart — hand it a serializable ChartSpec and it picks and renders the right chart.

name: BarChart
summary: Categorical comparison — composed from Bar + BarXAxis/BarYAxis inside its provider.

name: BumpChart
summary: Rank over discrete time — who is #1 changes over time. variant="lines" plots the trajectory (rank as an inverted y-axis); variant="strip" is the G21 filmstrip (fixed rows, shade + a printed number carry the per-period rank).

name: CanvasLayer
summary: The canvas mark path for ChartFrame — a drop-in sibling of the SVG marks for views past what the DOM can carry (~20k marks up), with a spatial-grid hit test and a one-tab-stop virtual cursor.

name: ChartCard
summary: Titled card surface around a chart — header, description, and the chart body.

name: ChartFrame
summary: Opt-in chart wrapper adding expand / flip-to-table / download-CSV to any chart child.

name: ChartLegend
summary: Series key with label, value and an optional progress bar; pattern-aware under decoration.

name: ChoroplethChart
summary: Region-shaded map for a measure that is defined per geographic area.

name: ComposedChart
summary: One cartesian frame that layers several series types (bars + lines + areas) together.

name: DistributionChart
summary: One numeric variable, optionally by group, read four ways on one shared scale — histogram, box, violin or strip.

name: DumbbellChart
summary: Before/after (or this-year/last-year) per category — a track with two markers and the delta between them, so the CHANGE is the mark, not a second bar. variant="slope" swaps the per-category track for two shared value columns.

name: EditorialMarks
summary: SVG text that punches a plot-ground halo out from behind itself, so a label stays readable directly ON a mark instead of beside it.

name: FunnelChart
summary: Stage-by-stage drop-off through an ordered pipeline.

name: Gantt
summary: Schedule grid — tasks as bars over time, with a task table beside them.

name: Gauge
summary: Single-value dial against a known range — a KPI with an explicit ceiling.

name: HeatmapChart
summary: Two discrete dimensions × one value — weekday × hour, product × region, or a year of days.

name: LineChart
summary: Trend over a continuous (usually time) axis.

name: MetricGrid
summary: Responsive grid of KPI tiles — the summary row at the top of a dashboard.

name: NetworkChart
summary: A node-link graph in three layouts — a settled force cloud, a ring of chords, or a bipartite colonnade — with hover/focus adjacency emphasis.

name: ParallelCoordinatesChart
summary: Same entities across 3-6 mixed-unit dimensions: one hairline per entity threaded through per-axis-normalized vertical scales, so shape and crossing pattern reveal correlation across axes that share no common unit.

name: PieChart
summary: Part-of-whole split across a handful of categories.

name: RadarChart
summary: Multi-metric profile comparison on a shared radial axis.

name: SankeyChart
summary: Flow diagram — how quantity moves between stages or nodes.

name: ScatterChart
summary: Point cloud for correlation between two continuous measures.

name: SeriesPattern
summary: Categorical comparison — composed from Bar + BarXAxis/BarYAxis inside its provider.

name: Sparkline
summary: Tiny, axis-less trend that lives inside a KPI tile or a table cell.

name: Tooltip Presets
summary: Hover readout for the point/series under the pointer.

name: TreeChart
summary: Fixed-spacing, left-to-right (or top-to-bottom) orthogonal hierarchy diagram — every node the same visual weight, no sizes: 'who belongs to whom'.

name: TreemapChart
summary: Two-level squarified treemap — a hierarchy where area, not position, encodes value.

name: UnitChart
summary: One mark = one honest unit — waffle grid, phyllotaxis field or tick rows, so a share is COUNTED rather than judged by angle or area; lieflat's default replacement for a pie.

name: WaterfallChart
summary: Gross-to-net bridge: running-total steps and subtotal bars showing what added and subtracted along the way.

name: A2UI Agent Ops
summary: The SAFE generative-UI path (D2): renders an agent-DESIGNED screen from data — a JSON tree of catalog types validated against the catalog — with the real components; actions reach the host's onAction.

name: A2UI Analytics
summary: The SAFE generative-UI path (D2): renders an agent-DESIGNED screen from data — a JSON tree of catalog types validated against the catalog — with the real components; actions reach the host's onAction.

name: A2UI Surface
summary: The SAFE generative-UI path (D2): renders an agent-DESIGNED screen from data — a JSON tree of catalog types validated against the catalog — with the real components; actions reach the host's onAction.

name: AgentEvent
summary: One lifecycle or hook event on the agent timeline — what fired around a tool call, and whether its checks passed.

name: AgentTimeline
summary: Chronological rail of agent steps and checkpoints — what the agent did, in order.

name: AlertDialog
summary: Confirmation overlay for destructive / irreversible actions — friction proportional to consequence.

name: AppIcon
summary: The standard app/brand mark for app chrome — theme-aware, morphs mark↔lockup on sidebar collapse.

name: ApprovalCard
summary: The named human-in-the-loop variant of Confirmation — a titled, described approval card, binary or N-option with scope.

name: AppSidebar
summary: The opinionated application sidebar: the Sidebar skeleton behind typed header and footer slots, with the navigation as children.

name: AssetPreview
summary: Type-keyed preview of ONE produced asset — markdown/code/sql/csv/image — inside the Artifact chrome.

name: AudioPlayer
summary: Themed audio transport for generated/recorded speech, built on media-chrome's MediaController.

name: AudioVisualizer
summary: Canvas-drawn live mic-level / waveform meter, driven entirely by a `levels` prop.

name: Badge
summary: Compact status/label chip (status, count, category).

name: BrandLogo
summary: The product's mark/lockup, drawn from tokens so it adapts to every theme.

name: Button
summary: Primary action trigger — the canonical way to invoke an action.

name: Canvas
summary: The in-chat agent workspace graph surface (React Flow) — the canvas an agent renders inside a conversation (ADR 0018).

name: CanvasShell
summary: Branded React Flow canvas wrapper with token-driven background + sane defaults.

name: Card
summary: Surface grouping related content into a bordered, padded block.

name: ChatGreeting
summary: The centered, display-scale first-run greeting for an empty chat scene — a headline, not a status message.

name: Checkbox
summary: Binary on/off toggle within a form (multi-select within a group).

name: CodeBlock
summary: Shiki-highlighted code block with a copy button, filename and language selector.

name: CodeEditor
summary: Monaco-backed editable code editor (controlled/uncontrolled), themed from tokens.

name: Combobox
summary: Searchable single/multi select — Select with typeahead over a large or async option set.

name: Composer
summary: The standard chat input — a PromptInput pre-assembled with attachments, tools and submit.

name: ContextPanel
summary: The chat workspace's right context rail — sources, produced assets and a root↔detail drill-in.

name: Conversation
summary: Auto-stick-to-bottom chat transcript region.

name: CTASection
summary: Closing conversion band — one message, one action.

name: Dashboard
summary: The classic left-sidebar dashboard: a collapsible-icon nav rail with a tenant switcher and nav groups beside a floating inset surface carrying a metric row, a revenue trend and an overnight activity feed. Skip link, one main landmark, active-route indicator and command trigger included.

name: Dashboard sheet app
summary: The installable canonical full-screen, user-editable dashboard: app nav + DashboardToolbar + DashboardSelectionBar + asset/properties panels + DashboardSheet, with the table/chat/process-map tile blocks registered alongside the built-in kinds.

name: DataTable
summary: TanStack-backed data grid with sorting, filtering, pagination and a render-prop toolbar.

name: Dialog
summary: Modal overlay for focused tasks/flows that block the page until dismissed.

name: DiffEditor
summary: The Monaco side-by-side diff surface — the only diff in the library that can be typed into.

name: DiffView
summary: A line-level unified diff inside an agent transcript — what the agent changed, with correct old/new line numbers.

name: Double-Sided
summary: Two navigation levels plus a summoned third surface: a permanent 56px icon rail picks the area, a collapsible second panel lists that area's sections, and the floating inset carries the settings screen. A resizable right-hand SideDock holds the change history — a column above 1100px, an overlay below it. The icon rail is deliberately not a Sidebar, so it survives every breakpoint while the section panel becomes a sheet.

name: Factory Plan
summary: The key to a plan's status channels — the tone swatch, the outline style and the word, so the textures and dashes on the canvas mean something.

name: FeatureGrid
summary: Grid of capability cards below the hero.

name: FileTree
summary: Hierarchical file/folder list for a workspace — `code` (IDE source tree) or `document` (produced assets) look.

name: FileViewer
summary: Render a file the app did not write (upload, signed URL, agent output) — detects the format, loads the matching adapter on demand, draws it with brand-ui components.

name: Flagship
summary: Sidebar + top nav + page layout scaffold for an internal app.

name: FlowNode
summary: Branded custom React Flow node (title/subtitle/kind/icon/tone).

name: Gallery
summary: Image/asset grid with a +N overflow tile that opens a lightbox Dialog (carousel + metadata).

name: GroupedParts
summary: Renders an ordered message part list, folding adjacent reasoning/tool parts into collapsible traces.

name: Hero
summary: Above-the-fold marketing headline, subcopy and the primary call to action.

name: Icon
summary: The brand/product-vocabulary icon primitive — 24×24, stroke = currentColor, so it themes with text.

name: Input
summary: Single-line text field — the base form input.

name: InteractiveTerminal
summary: Streaming terminal surface for agent shell output, with an optional input line.

name: KeyboardShortcuts
summary: Grouped, searchable presentation of an application's shortcut set — the sheet the Kbd atom belongs in.

name: Mail
summary: Three-zone mail shell: the collapsible icon rail, a searchable message list, and a reading pane sharing one floating inset surface. A variation on the dashboard shell, not a separate idea; below md the two content zones become a drill-down.

name: MapCanvas
summary: Root MapLibre canvas — theme-aware basemap; the ref is the raw MapLibre Map. With `plan` it is a non-geographic plan instead (a floor, a plant, a carriage) and every layer inside speaks plan units.

name: MapClusterLayer
summary: Clusters dense point data into count bubbles that split apart as you zoom in.

name: MapMarker
summary: A point on the map, optionally carrying content, a label, a popup or a tooltip.

name: MarkdownView
summary: Branded, read-only renderer for a produced markdown document (not a code view).

name: MessageCompare
summary: Side-by-side 2-4 column comparison of model responses to the same prompt — the one-at-a-time sibling of MessageBranch.

name: MessageEdit
summary: Edit-in-place for a user message — swaps the bubble between content and an editor.

name: MessageFeedback
summary: Thumbs up/down on a single assistant message.

name: MessageForm
summary: A model-emitted, zod-validated form rendered inside a chat message; returns structured values on submit.

name: MessageTable
summary: A model-emitted, column-oriented data table rendered as message content.

name: MetricCard
summary: Single KPI tile — label, value, delta/trend.

name: ModelProviderLogo
summary: The mark of an AI model provider, sized for a row in a model list.

name: PermissionModeSelect
summary: Standing permission-policy chooser — how far the agent may act on its own, not whether one call proceeds.

name: Persona
summary: The animated agent avatar/presence mark (Rive), used as the assistant's identity.

name: Plan
summary: A Card-shaped, collapsible plan the agent proposes before it starts executing — and the decision the human returns.

name: Plan Maps
summary: The keyboard and label layer of a plan: one real <button aria-pressed> per region over the WebGL canvas, with spatial arrow-key travel and a group mode for very large plans.

name: Popover
summary: Anchored, dismissible floating panel for lightweight contextual content.

name: ProcessMap
summary: Directly-follows process map: activities as nodes, transitions as edges, both painted from one metric choice, with an accessible table twin.

name: PromptInput
summary: Chat composer FORM (Enter submits) emitting a message to the app's runtime.

name: PromptInputEffort
summary: Composer control for an ordered reasoning-budget scale whose indicator fills as the level rises.

name: PromptInputMode
summary: Composer control for the agent's operating mode — an app-defined enum of how autonomously it may act.

name: PromptInputSlash
summary: The slash-command palette over a composer — type `/`, filter by prefix, pick a command with the keyboard.

name: RadioGroup
summary: Mutually-exclusive single choice from a small visible set.

name: SearchInput
summary: Controlled search box that drives a DataTable's global filter.

name: Select
summary: Single-choice dropdown from a known set of options.

name: SelectionToolbar
summary: A floating toolbar over selected transcript text, offering Quote as the default action.

name: SessionHeader
summary: Session launch card — model, workspace, capabilities, what's new and quick actions, shown above the greeting in an empty session.

name: SessionStatusBar
summary: Ambient session row — workspace, branch, model and integration-connection progress, docked above or below the transcript.

name: Sheet
summary: Edge-anchored panel (left/right/top/bottom) for secondary flows beside the page.

name: StatusBadge
summary: The closed seven-state execution-status vocabulary, each state carrying its own icon as well as its own tone.

name: Switch
summary: Immediate on/off setting toggle (applies on change, not on submit).

name: Tabs
summary: Switch between peer views in the same context without navigating away.

name: Terminal
summary: Read-only ANSI console output with copy/clear actions and stick-to-bottom streaming.

name: TerminalBanner
summary: The console-dress launch card above an empty transcript: identity (name, model, version, workspace), capabilities, what's new and quick actions with key hints — every section independently optional.

name: TerminalComposer
summary: The prompt composer for the agent-session family: a text input well, an optional mode indicator, an optional ordered effort scale, a shortcut-hint row, and a submit affordance that becomes a stop affordance while busy.

name: TerminalConsole
summary: The console FRAME (ADR 0033): the one resting surface a coding-agent console draws — edge, radius, ground and elevation — so a transcript, banner, permission prompt, composer and status bar sit inside it as flush regions separated by a single seam instead of as separately framed cards.

name: TerminalDiffHunk
summary: An inline unified diff hunk in console dress: a header naming the file, then one row per line — a line-number column, a polarity marker, and the line text — with a collapsed run of context lines behind a real disclosure.

name: TerminalEventLine
summary: The CLI dress of an agent lifecycle/hook event line: a fixed marker glyph, a label, and an optional phase/hook-count/duration, sharing AgentEvent's outcome and hook-count model so the two skins stay in sync.

name: TerminalOverlay
summary: The console-dress modal frame: a real Radix Dialog painted on the terminal ground, with a title row, arbitrary caller content, and an optional key-hint legend along the bottom — a frame, not a catalogue of panels.

name: TerminalPermission
summary: The per-call scoped approval prompt: title, command preview, question, then numbered options whose SCOPE (once/session/deny) is stated in real label text and chosen through a real Radix RadioGroup, never a hand-rolled focus walk.

name: TerminalSlashMenu
summary: The `/`-command palette for the console composer: a popover listbox anchored to TerminalComposer's own textarea, filtered by prefix, navigated with wrapping/clamped arrow keys, and spliced into the text on Enter — the caret never leaves the field.

name: TerminalStatusBar
summary: The ambient chrome row along the bottom of a console surface: branch and working directory on the left, connection/context/turn progress on the right, every fact independently optional.

name: TerminalSurface
summary: The console ground for the agent-session family: the terminal surface, the mono type role and the two-column gutter grid, established once and published to every row inside.

name: TerminalTodoList
summary: A three-state checklist (done/active/pending) rendered as a real <ol>/<li>, where each row's state is a glyph AND an announced word riding TerminalRow's gutterLabel, so it survives greyscale and reaches assistive tech.

name: TerminalToolCall
summary: A single tool invocation dressed as a CLI line: a status glyph (success/error/pending), the tool name plus its optional argument in parentheses, a result summary on a `⎿` row, and detail behind a real disclosure.

name: TerminalTranscriptRow
summary: One line of an agent transcript on top of TerminalRow: a closed kind axis (user/agent/output/error) that carries who spoke and whether it failed as a glyph, a colour and an accessible label.

name: TerminalWorking
summary: The in-turn footer row pinned last in a transcript: a spinner/diamond glyph, a label, elapsed time, token spend and a stop control — the three facts and an exit the human needs while the agent runs.

name: Tile — Chat
summary: A DashboardTileKind wrapping @elabs-ai/components-ai's ChatShell/Composer: the composer is disabled when the sheet's interactions.active is false.

name: Tile — Process map
summary: A DashboardTileKind wrapping @elabs-ai/components-process's ProcessMap: the sheet's tri-state selection maps 1:1 onto ProcessMap's own selectionStates, and a node click emits that activity as the tile's selection.

name: Tile — Table
summary: A DashboardTileKind wrapping @elabs-ai/components-data's DataTable: selection tri-state dims/frames excluded rows, a row click toggles that row's field value into the sheet's selection.

name: Toolbar
summary: A dense row of controls that acts on nearby content, collapsed into ONE tab stop with arrow-key navigation between the controls.

name: ToolResultCard
summary: The artifact a tool PRODUCED, presented as the headline — raised surface, no border, children carry the payload. Its header row is title | actions | status, where actions are scoped to the whole artifact (expand, download, open).

name: Tooltip
summary: Transient hover/focus hint with supplementary (non-essential) text.

name: Train Carriage
summary: The keyboard and label layer of a plan: one real <button aria-pressed> per region over the WebGL canvas, with spatial arrow-key travel and a group mode for very large plans.

name: TurnStatus
summary: In-turn footer reporting the three facts a running turn owes the user: elapsed time, cost, and how to stop it.

name: ViewToolbar
summary: The row above a list, table or board — status and filters on the left, actions on the right, every control its own tab stop.

name: WorkspacePicker
summary: Choose the workspace or project directory a session runs against, from recents or a typed path.

name: Agent Operations Center
summary: The control room for a fleet of AI agents: the agent-ops block family as one product across four tabs — insight feed, spend against limit and the escalation boundary; the trace waterfall and handoff inspector; a run review and a decision record; the audit log — with every block callback wired and the review count reflected in the navigation, the tab and the header.
question: For teams running AI agents in production

name: Agentic AI Workspace
summary: A full-page demo scenario composed from the @elabs-ai/components-* grammar: a double-sided application shell (collapsible left nav + the real ContextPanel right rail with animated collapse and asset drill-in) wrapping a complete agentic AI interaction — reasoning, a plan, the AgentTimeline execution rail, tools with JSON behind disclosure, a ToolResultCard chart headline, an ApprovalCard decision, a task summary, a checkpoint, and a grounded AgentMessage answer with an EvidenceChip and a SourceList.
question: For copilots and agentic products

name: Customer 360
summary: One account before the call: a record header, four MetricCards (one with a commitment-marked Meter), usage against the contract as a LineChart with a labelled rule, a self-explaining health score, a RadarChart against peers, next actions completed in place, an activity Timeline and the people with the relationship gap stated in the title, plus a docked account brief.
question: For account, success and CRM products

name: Enterprise Admin Console
summary: The baseline-complete archetype-B console — the recommended starting point for a professional brand-ui app.

name: Incident Command
summary: One live incident run from one screen: severity, impact and commander in the header, a streaming LiveLineChart of the error rate, an AreaChart with the SLO as a labelled rule, the dependency-web block for blast radius, and a runbook whose steps print into a Terminal, tick off, move a Meter and write the incident log. Steps run in order; the last one settles the stream and unlocks Resolve.
question: For reliability, observability and platform teams

name: Logistics Control Tower
summary: The screen an operations team keeps open all day: a headline computed from the exceptions, the network and fleet map blocks behind tabs, and an exceptions DataTable sorted by the closest promise whose row click summons the dock with the shipment's Descriptions, the recommended next step and its journey as a Timeline. The controlled-dock master-detail pattern for the workspace shell.
question: For supply-chain, fleet and field-operations teams

name: Market Desk
summary: Watch the market, then act on it: the market-tape command center as the read side, a watchlist DataTable whose row click pre-fills the ticket, and a docked order ticket that is a real form — FieldRoot validation in the trader's terms, a NumberInput, a computed commitment checked against a limit, a review step before anything is placed, and a blotter that fills as orders go in.
question: For pricing, trading and treasury products

name: Object Detail Hub
summary: The canonical master-detail enterprise screen: a searchable object list (SplitPanel start) drives a detail HUB (end) with a sticky SectionHeader identity + status, a ButtonGroup toolbar, Tabs for the object's sections (Overview / Activity / Settings), Descriptions for attributes, a related-runs list, and a high-value Run task promoted to its own Dialog.

name: Process Explorer
summary: A map-first process-mining workspace over an order-to-cash log: the six KPIs as one ribbon, every control in a toolbar so nothing floats over the map, and beside the map a panel of statistical insights — throughput distribution against the SLA, the slowest hand-overs, the weekly trend, box and violin plots by region and channel — plus variants as colour strips, the selected element and deviations. A dock holds the dotted chart, the performance spectrum, the workload heatmap and the case table; a replay animates every order as a token. One useProcessExplorer instance drives all of it, so no two panels can disagree.
question: For process-mining and operations-excellence tools

name: Project Hub
summary: Projects, the issue board, team load and members as one product: the workspace shell's navigation swaps views in place, the project-cards, kanban-board and settings-members blocks do the work, one dock explains the project or issue last opened, and every view reads the same issues so a move on the board changes the load, the overview and the navigation counts.
question: For project, issue-tracking and delivery tools

name: Revenue Operations
summary: An analytics workspace for revenue, finance and BI teams: the workspace shell with a summoned analyst, a page header whose period and region controls re-slice the charts and the pipeline, the revenue command center as the body, and a pipeline DataTable with a win-probability Meter, an activity Sparkline, a computed Stalled flag and row selection feeding a bulk action.
question: For revenue, finance and BI teams

name: Support Desk
summary: Queue, conversation, context: a three-pane surface in the workspace shell laid out by container queries, a queue sorted by the promise that breaks first with a Meter per row, a conversation from the ai package's Message parts, a copilot draft grounded in named past tickets that you send or discard, and a context pane with the promise, the customer and what solved it before. Sending a reply restarts the clock and re-sorts the queue.
question: For support, service and helpdesk products

name: Terminal Agent Session
summary: The coding-agent CLI look-alike family (@elabs-ai/components-terminal, #117)
